fixes.explanation: I get why you'd think a little breeze sneaks through, friend. But the angels are holding back the four winds "…so that no wind would blow on land or sea or on any tree." (Revelation 7:1) Not a big wind, not a small one, not even a lazy puff.

Right, friend. The four angels are holding back the winds "…so that no wind would blow on land or sea or on any tree." (Revelation 7:1) That means no breeze at all, not even a tiny one. A leaf up there wouldn't get to wiggle.

That sounds like a fair guess, but it's not what the text says. John says these four angels "…had been given power to harm the land and the sea…" (Revelation 7:2) They're standing at the four corners of the earth, not at the throne.
You've got it, friend. The angel says, "Do not harm the land or sea or trees until we have placed a seal on the foreheads of the servants of our God." (Revelation 7:3) So the sealing comes first.

That's a small circle, friend, and this crowd is much wider. John sees a multitude "…from every nation and tribe and people and tongue…" (Revelation 7:9) Nothing in this verse limits it to towns near Jerusalem.

The elders are in the scene, friend, so I see how you got there. But the crowd cries out, "Salvation to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!" (Revelation 7:10) The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29). He's the one named next to the One on the throne.

Right, friend. The text says the angels "…fell facedown before the throne and worshiped God…" (Revelation 7:11) That's all the angels, standing around the throne, the elders and the four living creatures. Then they start speaking their praise.

You got it, friend. One of the elders asks John, "These in white robes, who are they, and where have they come from?" (Revelation 7:13) So the elder asks both who they are and where they came from. The elder gives the answer a moment later.

Babylon, friend? Big name in the Bible, but it never shows up in this verse. The elder says, "These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation…" (Revelation 7:14) Those are the words the text gives. I spent years in a junk drawer losing track of what day it was, so I'm the last one to judge a mix-up.
That's right, friend. The elder says, "they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb." (Revelation 7:14) That's the washing the verse names.

Yes, friend. The elder says the Lamb "…will lead them to springs of living water…" (Revelation 7:17) That's the first blank, and it goes with the promise that they will never thirst. (Revelation 7:16) The Lamb is their shepherd, and He does the leading.

Bread is a good guess, friend, since it goes with the promise that they will never hunger. (Revelation 7:16) But the elder says the Lamb will lead them "…to springs of living water…" (Revelation 7:17) So the first blank is water. Bread isn't in the verse.

A cloud would be some shade from the heat, friend, so I see the thinking. But the verse says God will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and that the Lamb will lead them to springs of living water. (Revelation 7:17) Cloud isn't in it.
